comparison: Both strongly support the mwSuMD methodological contribution (C2, C10, C40, C49, C52-C57). OpenEval emphasizes algorithmic documentation and novelty (C3), while peer reviewers highlight wide applicability and compatibility with MD engines. High agreement on method validity.

Both support the systematic parameter comparison and RMSD measurements (C14-C17, C41, C43-C45). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment, peer reviewers accept the validation evidence without critique. Strong concordance on methodological benchmarking.

Both support the GDP release mechanism (C35-C39, C47-C48). OpenEval notes limited statistical confidence (1/3 successful replicas) but finds claims appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers accept this as significant achievement with experimental support. Agreement despite OpenEval's statistical caveat.

Divergent evaluations of ligand binding and activation pathway (C22-C26). OpenEval finds claims supported with good RMSD agreement to experimental structures. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting results largely reproduce known structures without significant advances. Key disagreement on novelty vs. validation.

Both address efficiency improvements and mechanistic observations (C20-C21, C42). OpenEval supports speed claims and ECL involvement. Peer reviewers accept methodological advantages but suggest novel residue predictions (C18-C19, grouped by peer) require validation through in silico mutagenesis. Partial agreement.

Both support protein-protein binding capabilities (C27, C29-C30). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative agreement and contrast with failed classic MD. Peer reviewers accept this as demonstrating rare event sampling capability. Strong agreement on method effectiveness despite limited sample size.

Both address novel residue predictions (C18-C19). OpenEval supports these as hypothesis-generating results from simulation data. Peer reviewers group with C20-C21, C42 and suggest validation is advisable, expressing uncertainty. Moderate disagreement on sufficiency of current evidence.

Overlapping claims on G protein binding (C31-C32). OpenEval expresses uncertainty due to high RMSD values and limited convergence (2/3 replicas). Peer reviewers support the overall demonstration of complex binding process sampling. Divergent confidence levels.

Both address D344-R385 interaction (C34). OpenEval rates overall G protein results as uncertain due to high RMSDs but notes mutagenesis support for C34. Peer reviewers specifically highlight C34 as having novel insight potential but requiring validation. Agreement on need for additional support.

Both address future applications (C50). OpenEval supports this as appropriately qualified speculation about transition pathway analysis. Peer reviewers support broad applicability claims (C50-C51) for computational biology community. Agreement on forward-looking potential.
OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1, C4-C9, C11-C13, C28) as appropriately cited established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval supports methodological tool citations (C58-C59) as standard, well-documented computational methods. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Minor overlap on C33 (G protein conformational changes). OpenEval groups C33 with other G protein binding results rated as uncertain. Peer reviewers group C33 with activation pathway claims, noting reproduction of known structures. Both express reservations about novelty.

Minimal overlap on novelty claim C3. OpenEval includes C3 in supported methodological development group. Peer reviewers implicitly accept novelty through positive assessment of GDP release mechanism. Indirect agreement.
